title: NIST SP 800-53
summary: NIST Special Publication 800-53 is the United States federal control catalogue for information systems and organisations, and it has become the de facto reference control set for regulated industries well beyond government. Its structure is what makes it useful to engineers: controls are grouped into families such as Access Control, Audit and Accountability, Configuration Management, Incident Response, Risk Assessment and Supply Chain Risk Management, and each control carries a statement, supplemental guidance, assessment procedures drawn from SP 800-53A, and optional control enhancements that allow an organisation to dial specificity up or down. Controls are selected and tailored through the SP 800-37 risk management framework process, where a system is categorised for confidentiality, integrity and availability impact, a control baseline is chosen, and the resulting set is documented in a system security plan with a plan of action and milestones for anything not yet satisfied. The critical practitioner insight is that 800-53 is a catalogue, not a compliance regime by itself: it becomes mandatory through law, contract or agency policy, and the burden of evidence sits with the organisation. Control identifiers are stable and widely reused, which is why so many commercial and cloud compliance mappings, including the FedRAMP baselines, are expressed as 800-53 selections. Teams that implement it well automate evidence collection against assessment procedures rather than treating the catalogue as a documentation exercise.
objectives: You will be able to explain how categorisation, baseline selection and tailoring produce a system-specific control set.
You will be able to read a control family and its enhancements and translate them into implementable configuration.
You will be able to build evidence that satisfies SP 800-53A assessment procedures for audit and accountability controls.
You will be able to author a system security plan with an honest plan of action and milestones.
You will be able to map 800-53 controls to ISO 27001 Annex A and NIST CSF Subcategories to reuse existing work.
You will be able to spot where an inherited control from a cloud provider does not transfer accountability.

sources.label: NIST SP 800-53 security and privacy controls

beginner.definition: NIST SP 800-53 is a large catalogue of security controls published by the National Institute of Standards and Technology in the United States. A control is a safeguard, such as an access rule or a log review. The controls are grouped into families like access control, incident response and supply chain risk. It is a menu, not a law.
beginner.whyItMatters: Teams waste months rewriting the same safeguards in different words for each customer. A shared control catalogue lets you describe your work once and reuse it. It also helps you find what you forgot, because the families cover areas people often miss. The catalogue becomes binding through a contract, a law or an agency rule.
howItWorks: Decide how much harm a loss of confidentiality, integrity or availability would cause.
Pick a starting set of controls that matches that level of harm.
Adjust the set for your situation, removing or adding controls as needed.
Write a plan that says who owns each control and how it is implemented.
List anything not yet finished, with a date and a named owner.
Collect evidence that shows each control works, then review it often.
beginner.example: Think of a building code. It lists rules for wiring, stairs and fire doors, but the city decides which rules apply to your building. A small warehouse follows fewer rules than a hospital. An inspector then checks your building against the list. NIST SP 800-53 works like that list for computer systems, and your own rules decide how much of it you must follow.
takeaways: NIST SP 800-53 is a catalogue of controls, not a law on its own.
You tailor the control set to your system and its risk level.
Unfinished controls still need an owner, a date and a plan.

exercises.title: NIST SP 800-53 - EASY
exercises.summary: Recall and recognition: definitions, one clear answer, single-step questions.

exercises.title: NIST SP 800-53 - MEDIUM
exercises.summary: Application: read a short log or alert and choose the correct next step.

exercises.title: NIST SP 800-53 - HARD
exercises.summary: Analysis: a multi-step scenario with distractors, evidence to weigh, and a reason to give.

exercises.title: NIST SP 800-53 - EXTREMELY HARD
exercises.summary: Synthesis under pressure: incomplete evidence, competing priorities, and a decision you must defend.
